wake2_native_task_read.title: HFO X12 Durable Object PDCA Lab

experiment.hypothesis: Across four wakes, the task contract fingerprint and exact task binding should remain stable even if the underlying carrier instance changes. Provider runtime timestamps may advance, but they do not identify the carrier.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: A later wake with the same task ID returns a different task-contract or schedule digest without an authorized task mutation; a provider-exposed carrier field changes but is suppressed; runtime timestamps fail to progress across a completed wake; a duplicate idempotency key is accepted; a stale version advances; or event/CURRENT readback fails.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: The provider runtime timestamps advanced, but they describe scheduler/task-record bookkeeping and the prior completed wake, not the identity of the carrier executing this wake. The native surface still does not expose model build, worker instance, conversation identity, or Project context, so no distinct-carrier claim is supported. Stable task metadata can mask carrier changes. The event and CURRENT pointer are separate Git commits, and Slack follows both; GitHub's single-file blob-SHA guard does not provide cross-file atomicity, database isolation, exactly-once execution, or transactional Slack durability.
canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable event or Slack message. If later invalidated, append a compensating event from the then-current version and replace CURRENT only using that pointer file's exact then-current blob SHA.
